text:
The Mammoth may be the best team in the West that doesn't feel like one. Utah has taken 56% of the expected goals and 58% at five on five, and it creates 3.58 expected goals per 60 minutes while allowing 2.79. The record, 10-6-1, is fine. It should be better.

The reason is in net. Utah has allowed 59 goals against 47.7 expected, more than 11 goals worse than its chances, and Karel Vejmelka has a .826 save percentage over his last five starts, 8.3 goals worse than expected, with one win in those five. The skaters are holding up their end. Their goalie hasn't held up his.

Up front, the line nobody would have picked is the best one: Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton have won 75% of the expected goals in 86 minutes. Logan Cooley has 15 points in his last 10 games against 9.6 expected, so he is both hot and genuinely producing. MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev eat the big minutes, 216 of them together, and win 58% of the chances even though the goals against them read 5-10.

Our simulations already see through it: a 100-point projection and an 86% playoff chance. If the saves come back to average, the Mammoth could pull away in the Central.
headline: Utah is good. Its goaltending isn't, lately
